paragraphs.text: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is an autosomal recessive disorder that appears within the first weeks of life. The intestine selectively fails to absorb dietary glucose and galactose. This leads to severe diarrhea and dehydration, which are usually fatal unless these sugars are removed from the diet (Turk et al., 1991). The disorder is caused by a defect in the intestinal Na+/glucose cotransporter SGLT1 (Martín et al., 1996).

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) studied a 3-year-old girl with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption, her family, and 16 normal volunteers. The proband's jejunal mucosa was unable to concentrate glucose throughout a 60-minute incubation period, but intestinal fructose accumulation was normal. She also had a partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption. Both parents and a half sister had intermediate impairment of glucose transport, whereas an asymptomatic brother had normal transport.

paragraphs.text: Elsas et al. (1970) showed that glucose transport by normal human jejunal mucosa was concentrative, saturable, and dependent on sodium and energy, and that it showed competitive inhibition. In the proband, absent intestinal glucose transport was accompanied by partial impairment of renal glucose transport. Fructose accumulation was similar in all subjects. In the jejunal mucosa of 3 heterozygotes, glucose influx was impaired, while glucose efflux was the same as in normal controls. Kinetic analysis showed reduced transport capacity (Vmax) with normal affinity (Km), suggesting that heterozygotes can be detected.

paragraphs.text: Turk et al. (1993) noted that a missense mutation in the SGLT1 gene caused autosomal recessive glucose/galactose malabsorption in 2 patients. In vitro, the resulting asp28-to-asn (D28N) substitution abolished SGLT1 transport activity.

checks.claim: A missense mutation in the SGLT1 gene caused autosomal recessive glucose/galactose malabsorption in 2 patients.
checks.evidence_quote: In two patients with the autosomal recessive disease glucose/galactose malabsorption, the underlying cause was found to be a missense mutation in SGLT1

checks.claim: The SGLT1 missense mutation in these glucose/galactose malabsorption patients results in an asp28-to-asn (D28N) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: the Asp28-->Asn change was demonstrated in vitro to eliminate SGLT1 transport activity
checks.explanation: Asp28-->Asn is the same change as D28N.

checks.claim: In vitro, the SGLT1 D28N substitution abolished SGLT1 transport activity.
checks.evidence_quote: the Asp28-->Asn change was demonstrated in vitro to eliminate SGLT1 transport activity

paragraphs.text: Martín et al. (1996) noted that 2 sibs with GGM from a large consanguineous family had previously been shown to carry the D28N mutation in SGLT1, which accounted for the defect in sugar absorption. In prenatal screening of 2 later pregnancies in the family, exon 1 was PCR-amplified and tested for D28N by EcoRV digestion. A sib fetus was heterozygous and a cousin fetus was not a carrier. Both children were healthy without diarrhea at 2 years of age.

checks.claim: 2 sibs with glucose/galactose malabsorption from a large consanguineous family had previously been shown to carry the D28N mutation in SGLT1.
checks.evidence_quote: Two proband siblings with GGM were previously demonstrated to contain a missense mutation (D28N) in the Na(+)-dependent glucose/galactose cotransporter (SGLT1)
checks.explanation: Stated directly. The family is called large and consanguineous elsewhere in the abstract.

checks.claim: The SGLT1 D28N mutation accounted for the defect in sugar absorption in the 2 sibs with glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: a missense mutation (D28N) in the Na(+)-dependent glucose/galactose cotransporter (SGLT1) that accounts for the defect in sugar absorption

checks.claim: Prenatal screening was performed in 2 later pregnancies in the family carrying the SGLT1 D28N mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Prenatal screening for GGM was performed in two subsequent pregnancies in this large consanguineous family.
checks.explanation: "Subsequent" in the paper corresponds to "later" in the claim.

checks.claim: In prenatal screening for SGLT1 D28N, exon 1 of SGLT1 was PCR-amplified and tested for D28N by EcoRV digestion.
checks.evidence_quote: The first exon of the SGLT1 gene was PCR-amplified from genomic DNA and screened for the presence of the D28N mutation by EcoRV restriction digestion.

checks.claim: A sib fetus in the family with glucose/galactose malabsorption was heterozygous for SGLT1 D28N.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband's sibling was heterozygous and a cousin was not a carrier of the D28N mutation.

checks.claim: A cousin fetus in the family with glucose/galactose malabsorption was not a carrier of SGLT1 D28N.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband's sibling was heterozygous and a cousin was not a carrier of the D28N mutation.

checks.claim: Both prenatally screened children from the family with SGLT1 D28N were healthy without diarrhea at 2 years of age.
checks.evidence_quote: Both children at 2-years of age remain healthy and have had no diarrhoeal symptoms.

paragraphs.text: In 33 patients with GGM from a large Old Order Amish pedigree, Xin and Wang (2011) found a homozygous c.152A-G transition in the SLC5A1 gene, resulting in an asn51-to-ser (N51S) substitution. The variant was 1 of 4 homozygous missense variants (see also A411T, R558H, and H615Q) that cosegregated with the GGM phenotype in all affected individuals.
